Recommendation (Para No. 3) 
 
The Committee appreciate the Ministry's efforts to mitigate the environmental 
impact of constructing new railway tunnels and bridges. Notably, the preference for 
elevated alignments to preserve ecology and wildlife as well as the use of steel, a recyclable 
material, for large -span bridges, demonstrates a commitment to sustainability. The 
Committee commend the initiative of constructing Amrit Sarovar by utilizing excavated 
earth from formation works. The Committee are of the view that this innovative approach 
not only ensures the productive use of surplus soil but also contributes significantly to 
water conservation and ecological balance within the p roject area. The Committee 
recognize that the concept of Amrit Sarovar aligns well with sustainable practices, such as 

 
 
18 
 
reducing earth disposal issues, promoting rainwater harvesting, aiding groundwater 
recharge, supporting local biodiversity and creating community water sources. While the 
Committee applaud the concept as sound and potentially highly valuable, its success 
depends on the quality of its execution, ecological planning and post -construction 
maintenance.  Therefore, the Committee strongly emphasize that Amrit Sarovar should not 
be treated as a mere checkbox activity or mere formality for compliance. Instead, it m ust 
involve thorough catchment planning, effective water retention measures, community 
participation and a long -term sustainable maintenance strategy. In light of its multiple 
environmental and community benefits, the Committee recommend that Ministry acti vely 
incorporate the development of Amrit Sarovar  into all major railway infrastructure 
projects, particularly in water-stressed and ecologically sensitive regions. 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched in April 2022 with the ambitious goal of 
constructing/rejuvenating 75 Amrit Sarovars  (ponds) in each district of the country. The 
guidelines for implementation of this mission were jointly issued by various Ministries of 
the Government including Railways. 
Mission Amrit Sarovar works have been taken  up by the States and Districts in 
convergence with the various ongoing schemes of the Government. The Mission has made 
significant contribution in addressing the critical issue of water scarcity and enhancing 
surface and groundwater availability across various regions. These Sarovars have not only 
addressed immediate water needs but also established sustainable water sources, 
symbolizing the commitment to long -term environmental sustainability and community 
wellbeing. 
Under this mission, approx. 21 lakh cubic metre of excavated earth/soil from 72 
Amrit Sarovars across the country was used for construction of new tracks. 
Now, Phase II of Mission Amrit Sarovar has been launched and guidelines dated 
24.02.2025 (ToC-959) have been jointly issued by Railways and M/o Rural Development 

 
 
19 
 
and it is envisaged to continue with a renewed focus on ensuring water availability, with 
community participation (Jan Bhagidaari) at its core, and aims to strengthen climate 
resilience, foster ecological balance, and deliver lasting benefits for future generations. 
Under this Phase II of the mission, Railways in coordination  with District 
Authorities have taken up identification of the location of New Amrit Sarovars from where 
excavated earth/soil can be taken for construction of formation of Railway Projects/Works. 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 4) 
 
The Committee note that Tunnel Management System (TuMS) has been developed 
in year 2024 -25 which is a positive step toward the digital management of tunnel 
infrastructure.  The Committee further note that the feeding of Indian Railways tunnel data 
into TuMS has been completed and data validation is currently underway, indicating 
proactive efforts in data management and quality assurance. The Committee desire the 
Railways to ensure regular updation and integrate inspection, maintenance and safety audit 
records into TuMS to enable real -time monitoring, predictiv e maintenance and timely 
decision-making for tunnel infrastructure safety and reliability. The Committee 
recommend the Ministry to expedite the completion of validation of data for all operational 
railway tunnels into the Tunnel Management System (TuMS) an d ensure its full 
operationalization at the earliest. 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
Tunnel master module (TuMS): The Tunnel Master  Module (TuMS) has  been 
developed as a specialized application under the Bridge Management  System (BMS) to 
comprehensively cover  all aspects related to the annual inspection, monitoring, and 
maintenance of railway tunnels. The module serves as a centralized digital platform for 
recording, updating, and analysing tunnel-related data across the Indian Railways network. 
Through TuMS, details such as tunnel geometry, structural components, lining 
condition, drainage arrangements, ventilation systems, and safety installations are 

 
 
20 
 
systematically captured and stored. The application also facilitates photographic 
documentation, condition assessment, and grading based on inspection parameters 
prescribed in the Indian Railways codes and manuals. 
Data entry in TuMS is being carried out on a regular basis by the concerned field 
units, ensuring that the inventory and condition  records remain current and authentic. 
Further, a process of data validation and cross -verification has been instituted to ensure 
the accuracy and reliability of the information being uploaded. 
By integrating TuMS with the broader BMS framework, the system enables holistic 
asset management, supports decision -making for maintenance planning, and helps in 
prioritizing rehabilitation or strengthening works. Thus, TuMS  represents a major step 
towards achieving digitally enabled, data -driven management of tunnel infrastructure on 
Indian Railways. 
Recommendation (Para No. 5) 
 
The Committee note that as per current norms, escape tunnels with adits  or lateral 
exits are provided for tunnels exceeding 3 km in length. The Committee also observe that 
certain existing tunnels, such as Tunnel No. 9 on the Lumding-Badarpur section (3.25 km), 
which carries both passenger and freight traffic, and Tunnel No. 57A on the Obulavaripalli-
Krishnapatnam section (6.63 km), used for goods trains, do not have escape tunnels. The 
Committee further note that the planning for Tunnel No. 9 was undertaken prior to the 
introduction of the policy mandating such provisions. Gi ven the critical importance of 
passenger and staff safety in case of emergencies, the Committee recommend that the 
Ministry examine the feasibility of providing escape tunnels or suitable alternative 
evacuation arrangements for all existing tunnels longer than 3 km. The Committee also 
urge that tunnels currently used exclusively for goods movement should be considered for 
escape tunnel provision, bearing in mind the potential future use for passenger traffic. 
Additionally, the Committee observe that Railway s is actively expanding its network in 
regions like the North East, Jammu & Kashmir and other mountainous areas where tunnels 
and bridges constitute a major part of the infrastructure. In light of this, the Committee urge 

 
 
21 
 
the Ministry to conduct a comprehensive review of all operational and under -construction 
railway tunnels — including those shorter than 3 km — with priority given to those located 
in vulnerable zones such as seismic areas, flood -prone stretches and regions  with 
challenging geology. Wherever feasible, the Ministry should consider the provision of 
escape routes, cross passages or alternative evacuation facilities to enhance safety measures 
and ensure preparedness for emergencies. Further, the Committee would like to be apprised 
of the findings of the team comprising representatives from the Railway Board, RDSO and 
NHAI which is examining the feasibility of utilising escape tunnels for road commuters to 
ensure optimum utilization of the infrastructure being developed. 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
Planning for Tunnel No. 9 on Lumding - Badarpur section was undertaken prior to 
the introduction of the policy mandating such provisions. The length is also only 250 m 
extra than the subsequently permitted length (3000m). However good approach road, 
ventilation, lighting and foothpath has been provided as alternative measures for safe 
evacuation. 
Tunnel No. 57A between Obulavaripalli– Krishnapatnam station is presently being 
used only for goods train. But Side pathways (footpaths) have been provided continuously 
on both sides along the entire length of the tunnel. These pathways serve as a safe and  
accessible passage for maintenance personnel in the event of any unforeseen circumstance, 
thereby functioning effectively as an evacuation corridor within the main tunnel itself. 
Moreover the escape tunnel/adits can be planned at later stages if need arises. 
The tunnels having length less than 3 km do not require a separate escape route or 
adits because the two portals (entrances) provide a quick exit for the passengers, and the 
maximum distance to a safe place is limited. However, the specific cases are dealt on need 
basis keeping in view of vulnerability of area such as seismic zones, flood prone stretches 
and region with challenging geology. 
An institutional mechanism for integrated planning of tunnel projects has been 

 
 
22 
 
formed jointly with the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway. Joint Working Group 
comprising representatives from the Ministry of Railways, MoRTH, and their respective 
executing agencies has been proposed for feasibility assessment of Rail -and-Road Tunnel 
Projects at Alignment - Finalization/DPR Stage. Gati Shakti Directorate is coordinating 
from Ministry of Railways. 
Comments of the Committee 
(Please see recommendation Para No. 10 of Chapter-I) 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 6) 
 
The Committee have reviewed the status submitted by the Ministry regarding the 
construction of Road Over Bridges (ROBs) and Road Under Bridges (RUBs) in major 
Indian cities for the replacement of existing level crossings. The Committee note that out 
of 305 level crossings in 46 cities with populations exceeding 10 lakh, works for 123 have 
been sanctioned. The Committee appreciate the continuous and dynamic approach adopted 
by Railways in sanctioning such works based on operational safety, mobility impact an d 
feasibility. However, the Committee are concerned over the slow pace of implementation 
and completion of these sanctioned projects, which is impeded by delays in land 
acquisition, utility shifting, encroachment clearance, statutory approvals and coordina tion 
with State Governments. Recognizing the critical importance of eliminating level crossings 
in congested urban areas for both rail safety and city traffic management, the Committee 
recommend that the Ministry devise a city -specific action plan in collaboration with State 
Governments and urban local bodies to fast -track pending ROB/RUB projects in major 
cities. The Committee further observe that delays in the construction and completion of 
such projects cause public inconvenience, resource wastage and co st escalation. The 
Committee urge the Ministry to ensure elimination of level crossing on National Highways 
on pilot project mode basis with clearly established timelines in coordination with 
NHAI/MORTH. The Committee also urge the Ministry to set clear ti melines, conduct 
periodic joint review meetings with all stakeholders and explore public-private partnership 

 
 
23 
 
(PPP) models to expedite the construction of these vital infrastructure projects, thereby 
ensuring seamless movement of both rail and road traffic. 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
Zonal Railways have been advised for expeditious construction of ROB/ RUBs in 
major cities falling in their jurisdiction in collaboration with State Governments and urban 
local bodies. 
In order to expedite completion & commissioning of ROB/RUB works, various steps 
have been taken: 
a) Land acquisition and removal of encroachments for ROB/RUBs has been 
covered under special railway projects as per Provisions of The Railway Act. 
b) Instructions have been issued to all zonal railways for entering into running 
contracts for timely identification of utilities and fixed structures coming in the 
alignment of ROB/RUB and their early shifting to fast track the construction of 
ROB/RUB Works. 
c) In ROB works, which are taken up on cost sharing basis, sometimes State 
Governments do not have the requisite funds, and are requesting Railways for 
bearing the 100% cost. Such proposals are being examined and 100% funding 
through Railways is being agreed on case to case basis. 
d) For expediting approvals and other matters, regular meetings are being held 
between Railway & State Government officials. Meetings are also being held 
with MORTH/NHAI on regular basis for addressing issues expeditiously. 
Further, monitoring of these issues is being done by Railway Board.  
e) For expediting NHAI/MORTH projects on National Highways, an online portal 
called “IR-Rail Road Crossing GAD Approval System” has been developed for 
real time monitoring of GAD approvals is presently being used by   
NHAI/MORTH/State agencies. The facility f or online approval of structural 
drawings has also been added in consultation with NHAI/MoRTH in the same 
portal. 

 
 
24 
 
f) For further improving the processes and to reduce delays in execution of works, 
a new portal for approval of QAP/WPSS and stage inspection of steel girder 
fabrication is under development. First phase of the portal, called “Portal for  
Rail Road Inspection & Stage Management – Steel Girder (PRISM -GS)” is 
already under implementation in field.  
 
Recommendation (Para No. 7) 
 
The Committee note the Ministry’s submission regarding the challenges faced in 
obtaining consent and financial participation from State Governments and Road Owning 
Authorities for the construction of Road Over Bridges (ROBs) and Road Under Bridges 
(RUBs) on a cost-sharing basis. The Committee appreciate the proactive approach of 
Railways in examining such cases and, wherever feasible and necessary, deciding to fully 
fund these projects in the interest of improving operational safety and train mobility. The 
Committee also note that 52 such cost -sharing projects have already been undertaken at 
100% railway cost. However, considering the critical importance of eliminating level 
crossings to enhance public safety and streamline train operations, the Committee 
recommend that the Ministry formulate a structured framework for prioritizing and 
independently funding such critical projects, wherever persistent delays arise due to non -
cooperation or lack of response from State Governments. Additionally, the Committee urge 
the Ministry to strengthen coordination mechanism with State Governments to secure 
timely consent and support for approach alignments, land acquisition and utility shifting. 
The Committee also recommend exploring alternative funding models including central  
assistance schemes for projects of high public utility and importance. 
 
Reply of the Government 
In ROB works, which are taken up on cost sharing basis, sometimes State 
Governments do not have the requisite funds, and are requesting Railways for bearing the 
100% cost. Such proposals are being examined and 100% funding through Railways is 

 
 
25 
 
being agreed on case to case basis. 60 nos such proposals have already been sanctioned on 
100 % funding by Railways.    
For expediting approvals and other matters, regular meetings are being held between 
Railway & State Government officials are carried out. Meetings are also being held with 
MORTH/NHAI on regular basis for addressing issues expeditiously. Further, monitoring 
of these issues is being kept by Railway Board.  
Recommendation (Para No. 8) 
 
The Committee note the Ministry’s policy framework for addressing the provision 
of Road Under Bridges (RUBs), Foot Over Bridges (FOBs) and pedestrian subways at 
locations where no level crossings (LCs) exist, but where public movement continues, 
either through existing roads leading up to the railway boundaries without LC or at sites 
where LC have been discontinued. The Committee observe that many such locations exist, 
particularly, where proper roads extend up to railway boundaries, yet serve as informal 
access points for trespassing. This situation results in recurring safety hazards, 
unauthorized crossings and potential disruption to train operations. The Committee 
recommend that the Ministry conduct a comprehensive joint survey of these locations 
across the railway network to assess safety risks, public demand and traffic density. This 
exercise should be carried out in coordination with State Governments, NHAI, and local 
civic bodies. Based on the survey findings, a time -bound action plan should be prepar ed 
for the provision of RUBs, limited or restricted height subways (LHSs), FOBs or pedestrian 
subways, wherever technically feasible and operationally essential on priority basis. 
Further the Committee desire that such infrastructure works be integrated with nearby road 
development or urban infrastructure projects to optimize resources utilization, improve 
public access to enhance operational and public safety. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
26 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
As per extant policy dated 19.08.2024, “If the location is a source of trespass, 
affecting safety in train operations, mobility of trains and fixed infrastructure of railway, 
Railway may consider providing suitable subways/FOB etc. as per feasibility at ra ilways 
cost”. Total 300 no. works have already sanctioned at non -Level Crossing locations to 
prevent trespassing.  
However, if any new development works are planned by State Government nearby 
track area, the work for construction of ROB/RUB at the demanded location may be taken 
up on deposit terms provided State Government agrees to bear the complete cost of 
construction and maintenance subject to its feasibility. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
(Please see recommendation Para No. 13 of Chapter-I) 
 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 9) 
 
The Committee note the various measures undertaken by Railways to ease traffic 
congestion and enhance safety at level crossings, including the progressive elimination of 
level crossings through the construction of Road Over Bridges (ROBs) and Road Under 
Bridges (RUBs), regular infrastructure upgradation such as maintenance of road surfaces, 
speed breakers, signage and widening where needed. The Committee appreciate the public 
awareness programs educating the dangers of unauthorized track crossings and promoting 
use of designated pathways. However, the Committee observe that despite complete 
elimination on unmanned level crossing and significant sale up during 2014 -2024 for 
complete elimination of the man level crossing, traffic congestion near several busy l evel 
crossings continues to be a persistent issue, particularly in urban and semi -urban areas. 
Therefore, the Committee urge the Ministry to intensify efforts to expedite sanctioning and 
execution of ROB/RUB projects and prioritize level crossings at high -traffic zones. 
Additionally, the Committee urge the Ministry to collaborate more closely with State 

 
 
27 
 
Governments, municipal bodies and road authorities to integrate railway crossing 
elimination works with local traffic decongestion and urban transport plans. Public 
awareness campaigns should be further expanded using modern communication strategies 
and community outreach to improve compliance and reduce trespassing and congestion 
near level crossings. 
Reply of the Government 
Traffic congestion at busy level crossings is a problem which affects the city 
dwellers as well as Railways. Due to congestion, it is sometimes difficult to close the level 
crossings in time which affects train operations. Zonal railways make regular effor ts to 
regulate the traffic and steps such as improving geometry, such as road widening, improve 
turning radius, removing obstructions such as poles etc.  
There is a lot of focus on sanctioning the works of ROB/RUBs for elimination of 
level crossings. As on 01.04.2025, 4402 Nos of works were sanctioned. This number has 
gone up to 4577 Nos works on date. 
For expediting approvals and other matters, regular meetings are being held between 
Railway & State Government officials. Meetings are also being held with MORTH/NHAI 
on regular basis for addressing issues expeditiously. Further, monitoring of these issues is 
being done by Railway Board. 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 10) 
 
The Committee note the various measures taken by Railways to address recurring 
water-logging problems in Road Under Bridges (RUBs) and subways, including 
integrating adequate drainage systems in new RUBs designs, diversion of water to nearby 
natural drains, provision of humps and cross drains, sealing of joints and installation of 
high-capacity pumps at vulnerable sites. The Committee also appreciate the provision of 
cover sheds at many locations and the systemati c inspection of RUBs before and after the 
monsoon to identify and resolve issues. However, despite these efforts the Committee 
observe that water-logging during heavy rainfall remains a significant problem in several 

 
 
28 
 
regions, causing traffic disruptions, safety hazards, and public inconvenience. The 
Committee recommend that the Ministry prepare a comprehensive inventory of all water -
logging prone RUBs and subways and prioritize remedial works in a time-bound initiative. 
Further, the Committee urge Railways to actively coordinate with municipal bodies and 
local authorities to ensure seamless integration of railway drainage with civic drainage 
systems. The Committee also desire the Ministry to establish a clear protocol f or 
temporarily halting road traffic during exceptionally heavy rainfall to safeguard 
commuters. 
Reply of the Government 
 
Railways have taken following remedial measures to mitigate the problem of water 
logging. 
• The inspection of Subways/RUBs is conducted before and after the onset of the 
monsoon. The monitoring of Subways/RUBs to prevent water logging is an 
ongoing process and redressal is undertaken whenever so warranted.  
• Adequate drainage arrangement has been made an integral part of planning of 
new Road under Bridge (RUB)/Subways.  
• To prevent waterlogging, the cover sheds over subways are being providing, 
pump capacity are being enhanced and size of sump are being increased. 
• An Action Plan has been prepared to prevent water logging in Subways/LHS. 
All deficiencies have already been rectified in 1351 nos. subways. 
• In order to provide relief to public in subways which are situated in 
waterlogging prone locations, instructions have been given for constructing 
additional Boxes of lesser depth.  An additional box of lesser depth is also being 
provided for the pedestrian in case of water logging. 
All above measures will help in addressing water-logging problems during rains. 
Comments of the Committee 
(Please see recommendation Para No. 16 of Chapter-I) 
 
 

 
 
29 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 11) 
 
The Committee note the initiatives by Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (GSV) bridge 
and tunnel engineering, including the ongoing B.  Tech program in Civil Engineering and 
the successful two -week specialized training on “Design, Fabrication, Launching, and 
Maintenance of Steel Girder Bridges,” benefitting officers from Indian Railways, PSUs, 
and other organizations. The Committee appreciate the proposal to start an M.  Tech 
program in Bridge and Tunnel Engineering from the academic year 2025 -26 and 
recommend the Ministry to ensure timely commencement of this program. The Committee 
also suggest introducing short -term certificate and diploma courses focused on modern 
technologies in bridge and tunnel construction and inspection. The Committee emphasize 
integration of Artificial Intelligence and technology in designing and monitoring 
techniques to build a specialized and skilled technical workforce equipped to manage the 
growing demands and challenges in railway bridge and tunnel infrastructure. Further, the 
Ministry should explore collaborations with specialized global institutes/organizations to 
develop curricula and programmes on cutting edge infrastructure technologies. The 
Committee emphasize that these initiatives will empower indigenous talent and reduce 
reliance on foreign consultants and contribute to more cost effective infrastructure 
development. 
Reply of the Government 
 
(1)  Ministry of Railways has accorded high priority to Bridge and Tunnel engineering 
aspect of railway functioning. Besides B.  Tech program in Civil Engineering, following 
courses have already commenced at GSV: 
• Short duration Training course on 'Design, Fabrication & Maintenance of Steel 
Girder Bridges'. 
• M.Tech program in Bridge and Tunnel Engineering. 
(2)  Further, GSV has been advised to disseminate the knowledge of bridge design and 
construction and to aid capacity building in following way: 
a) Short-term course (2-4 weeks) for Chief Bridge Engineers and their Teams as 

 
 
30 
 
well as officers involved in policy -making on 'Design and Inspection of Steel 
Girder Bridges, Subway Design'. 
b) GSV has further been advised to collaborate with potential Leading Institutes or 
Universities in course content and delivery covering areas of: 
• Modern inspection techniques, structural health monitoring, and underwater 
inspection methods for bridges, and 
• Accelerated construction and maintenance of subways, especially in 
challenging condition such as high water tables. 
c) Inclusion of visit to 4 iconic bridges of the SVDK -SGDN section as part of 2 -
year M.Tech Degree program on Bridge & Tunnel Engineering. 
d) Design of Short -term training program (2 -4 Weeks) capturing technical 
knowledge and practical learnings from USBRL Project, in coordination with 
subject experts involved in the project from KRCL, USBRL and Northern 
Railway. 
Recommendation (Para No. 12) 
The Committee observe that the construction of Road Over Bridges (ROBs) and 
Road Under Bridges (RUBs) faces significant challenges such as land acquisition, 
rehabilitation and resettlement issues, poor coordination among stakeholders, delays in 
approval of  General Arrangement Drawings (GADs), shifting of utilities, removal of 
encroachments and obtaining necessary statutory clearances. Moreover, cost -sharing 
complications particularly in the case of older sanctioned works which often result in 
stalled projects due to the absence of timely response from State Governments regarding 
their share also lead to delays.  The Committee note that as per existing norms, the portion 
of a ROB/RUB falling within railway land is to be maintained by the Railways, whereas 
the portion beyond railway limits, including the approach roads and lighting, falls under 
the maintenance responsibility of the concerned State Government/road-owning agency or 
local authority. The Committee express concern over the recurring issue of faulty designs, 
water-logging, public inconvenience and traffic stalling in RUBs and stress the need for 
long lasting solutions. While appreciating the efforts of the Railways in adopting 

 
 
31 
 
innovative designs to tackle water-logging and enhance user convenience, the Committee 
feel that more practical and sustainable solutions are required. In light of these challenges, 
the Committee desire the Ministry to establish a structured and institutio nal mechanism 
with proper implementation framework for the active involvement of people’s 
representatives during the planning and execution stages of ROB and RUB projects in a 
constituency.The Committee are of the considered opinion that their engagement will play 
a crucial role in addressing local concerns, ensuring early consensus for land acquisition 
and resettlement, facilitating smoother coordination with State and local authorities for 
utility shifting and clearances thereby help in timely completion and better maintenance of 
RUBs. The Committee are of the view that such participatory planning will lead to more 
efficient, transparent and community-responsive railway infrastructure development. 
Reply of the Government 
In order to address the problems related to land acquisition, rehabilitation and 
resettlement issues, poor coordination among stakeholders, delays in approval of General 
Arrangement Drawings (GADs), shifting of utilities, removal of encroachments and 
obtaining necessary statutory clearances, the system for sanction of works has been 
changed. Presently, the Detailed Project Report is being prepared for all the ROBs/RUBs 
prior to sanctioning of work. The due diligence is being at DPR stage, and various possible 
alternative options for alignment are being examined so that such problems are minimized 
during execution stage.  
The DPR preparation work includes Joint survey for fixing the alignment with road 
owning authorities, utility shifting, Resettlement and rehabilitation if any, approach 
gradients, number of lanes etc.  
Zonal Railways have also been advised for carrying out consultation with all stake 
holders while preparing DPR, and that representations from elected representative, if any, 
may also be considered for better appreciation of ground conditions. 
Comments of the Committee 
(Please see recommendation Para No. 19 of Chapter-I)

PART-I 
 
I.  INTRODUCTORY 
 
1.1  Indian Railways continues to serve as the backbone of the nation’s 
transportation system, connecting diverse regions and driving economic growth 
through its extensive and integrated network. Reflecting the Government’s sustained 
commitment to infrastructure expansion and modernization, the Capital Outlay for 
2026–27 has been pegged at Rs. 2,93,030 crore, which is Rs. 27,830 crore higher than 
the Revised Estimates for 2025 –26. The Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) has been 
fixed at Rs. 2,78,030 crore, supplemented by Rs. 3,000 crore from Internal Resources 
and Rs. 12,000 crore under Extra Budgetary Resources (Partnership).  
1.2 The Annual Plan for 2026 –27 places continued emphasis on removal of traffic 
bottlenecks, capacity augmentation and strengthening of safety infrastructure across 
the railway network. In pursuit of these objectives, substantial allocations have been 
made under Budgetary Sources in BE 2026 –27, including Rs. 36,722 crore for New 
Lines, Rs. 37,750 crore for Doubling works, Rs. 22,853 crore for Track Renewals, Rs. 
800 crore for Safety Works at Level Crossings, Rs. 8,225 crore for Road Over/Under 
Bridges (ROBs/RUBs) and Rs. 7,500 crore for Signal and Telecommunication works.  
The overall Capex allocated for capacity augmentation stands at Rs.1,13,670 crore, for 
customer amenities at Rs. 11,900 crore and for rolling stock and inventories at Rs. 
64,397 crore. 
1.3 Indian Railways have formulated the National Rail Plan (NRP) with the 
objective of creating a “future -ready” railway system by infrastructure augmentation. 
The Plan envisions meeting the growing demand for passenger and freight transport, 
segregating freight and passenger traffic on High Density Networks through 
Dedicated Freight Corridors, enhancing speeds of both freight and passenger trains, 
expanding connectivity to ports, mines and industrial clusters, and increasing the 
network to about 72,000 rou te kilometers. It also emphasizes induction of modern 

2 
 
rolling stock, redevelopment of 1,337 stations under the Amrit Bharat Scheme, 
implementation of advanced safety systems such as KAVACH, elimination of level 
crossings, adoption of predictive maintenance practices, 100% electrification and 
achievement of Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2030. 
1.4 Indian Railways have completed several landmark railway infrastructure 
projects aimed at enhancing regional connectivity and national integration. The 
Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (272 km) has been dedicated to the nation, 
ensuring seamless and all -weather connectivity of the Kashmir Valley with the rest of 
the country. The commissioning of the 51.38 km Bhairabi –Sairang New Line project 
through challenging hilly terrain has provided direct rail connectivity to Aizawl, the 
capital of Mizoram. Also, the inauguration of the New Pamban Bridge, the country’s 
first vertical lift sea bridge connecting Rameswaram Island to the mainland, marks a 
significant engineering achievement and strengthens connectivity in the southern 
region.

3.3 The main objectives and thrust areas of Annual Plan 2026 -27 are expanding, 
modernizing and enhancing the operational efficiency of the railway. The Ministry 
while detailing the main objectives and thrust areas remarked as under: 
 
A. Capacity Augmentation and Network Expansion: 
• New Lines (PH11) :  Construction of new rail lines presents a strategic 
avenue for enhancing last -mile connectivity. It contributes significantly 

7 
 
to economic development, particularly in remote areas, such as the 
Northeastern states and Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and 
Uttarakhand. New rail lines are planned to make travel easier within the 
country, helping people reach and leave areas that are difficult to 
access. Construction of new railway lines helps reduce congestion on 
existing routes by providing additional capacity for passenger and 
freight services. Improved transportation infrastructure attracts 
investment, support tourism, and enhance regional development. It also 
provides environmental benefits such as reduction of greenhouse gas 
emissions and contributes to a more sustainable and green 
transportation system by providing an alternative to road transportation. 
• Gauge Conversion (PH14)  :  Gauge conversion projects provide a 
uniform gauge for the smooth and fast flow of traffic, which is 
necessary for strategic and operating point of view. It improves the 
operational efficiency. 
• Doubling (PH15) :  The plan prioritizes the expansion of rail network 
capacity to meet the increasing demand for passenger and freight 
services. Projects for track doubling, tripling, and even quadrupling are 
underway to enhance line capacity. 
• Double-track railways use each track exclusively in one direction. This 
arrangement simplifies signaling systems. When one track of a double -
track railway is out of service due to track maintenance work or a train 
breaks down or during an unusual (Accident or ACF), all trains may be 
concentrated on a single usable track.  Maintenance 
and engineering work are easier on tracks in quadruple line with little 
resulting delay because standard double-track service can continue even 
if the other two double tracks are halted during the work. 
• Traffic Facilities (PH16) – Yard remodeling helps reduce congestion 
and improve the movement of passenger and freight trains. It involves 
interlocking of tracks to increase safety and capacity. Old yards were 
built for past needs, so remodeling removes issues like short shunting 

8 
 
necks and inadequate lines for cleaning or stabling trains. It also 
allows for more platforms to handle more trains, improving efficiency 
and reducing delays. Overall, yard remodeling is essential for 
improving railway infrastructure and making train services more 
reliable and efficient. 
• Dedicated Freight Corridors (PH61)  - Completion and 
operationalization of key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight 
Corridors to decongest the existing network. 
B. Modernization and Technological Upgradation: 
• Computerization (PH17)  : Updating mobile app services for 
passengers to improve the booking process and offer real -time train 
tracking.  Freight digitalization by online Indent placement, Supply 
information, Freight calculation and payment, Movement of receipt, 
Tracking of consignment, Detention charges (wharfage, demurrage) 
application. 
• Rolling Stock (PH21)  – Operationalization of coaches like; Vande 
Bharat, Amrit Bharat, LHB and Vande Sleeper, equipped with GPS, 
Wi-Fi, bio -toilets, and real -time information systems and upgraded 
interiors for enhancing passenger services. Acquisition of modern 
locomotives, exemplified by the WAG -12, represents a remarkable 
advancement in terms of power output and capabilities. Introduction of 
modern age wagons like Flat Multi -purpose Wagon, BCATIC and 
BLSS. 
• S&T Works (PH33)  - Advance signaling technologies such as 
Automatic Block Signaling (ABS) for  increased train frequency , 
KAVACH to avoid train collision etc. are useful in improving safety 
and efficiency. 
• Customer Amenities (PH53)  - Station Modernization by 
redevelopment of major railway stations under Amrit Bharat Station 
Scheme to provide world -class facilities to passengers. Modern Goods 

9 
 
Shed with high level platform, cover over platform, lighting and 
concrete pathways. 
• National High -Speed Rail Corporation Limited (PH61)  – Notable 
progress on Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project. 
C. Safety and Security: 
• Road Safety Works - LC/ROB/RUB (PH29/30) - Continuing efforts to 
eliminate all unmanned level crossings across the broad -gauge network. 
The closure of level crossings and the construction of Road Over 
Bridges (ROBs) or Road Under Bridges (RUBs) offer numerous 
benefits, contributing to enhanced safety, efficiency, and overall 
effectiveness of railway and road transportation systems. 
• Track Renewal/Bridge Works, Tunnel Works & Approaches  (PH31/32) 
- Significant investments in renewing old tracks, bridges and tunnels to 
enhance safety, Capacity, Operational Efficiency, Long -Term 
Durability and Passenger Experience. 
• Workshops including Production Units (PH42) – Workshops and PUs 
contribute to the overall performance of the rail network by facilitating 
timely repairs, maintenance, and production of rolling stocks. This, in 
turn, enhances the reliability and efficiency of the railway system, 
fulfils operational needs, enhance safety standards, and boost capacity 
and throughput. 
D. Electrification: 
• Electrification Projects (PH35) - Indian Railways aims to achieve 100% 
electrification. This is in line with the goal of reducing dependence on 
fossil fuels and making railways a greener, more sustainable mode of 
transportation. 
E. Sustainability and Green Initiatives: 
• Other Specified Works (PH64) - Projects include installation of solar 
power plants, rainwater harvesting systems and water recycling plants at 
stations and maintenance depots. 
F. Human Resource Development: 

10 
 
• Training/HRD (PH65) - Training programs to equip railway personnel with 
up-to-date skills and knowledge, preparing them to handle the complexities 
of modern railway operations. It leads to a more competent and efficient 
workforce to insure safety and operational efficiency. 
G. Urban Transport Integration: 
• Metropolitans Transport Project (PH81) - Expanding and improving 
suburban rail networks in major metropolitan areas to ease congestion and 
provide better connectivity for commuters. 
H. Freight Sector Development: 
• Encouraging public -private partnerships (PPPs) in freight operations, 
development of private freight terminals, and wagon leasing. 
I. Financial Sustainability and Resource Mobilization: 
• Monetization of Assets: Indian Railways plans to monetize assets like land, 
stations, and other infrastructure through long -term leasing and 
partnerships with private players. 
• Non-Fare Revenue: Increasing non -fare revenue through advertising, real 
estate development, and leasing of railway infrastructure.

IV. INTERNAL RESOURCES  
 
4.1 The Ministry while commenting on static year on year trend of Internal 
Resources detailed the action plan to meet the target of RE during the remaining 
period of 2025 -26 and concrete initiatives taken to increase the internal resources of 
the Railways as under :- 
• “Indian Railways incurred revenue expenditure of ₹ 2,63,018 crore in 
2024–25, with nearly 90% classified as inelastic and committed 
expenditure, increasing annually which includes establishment cost, 
pension, lease, fuel charges etc. 
• Passenger services are highly subsidized, with an average concession of 
about 45%, and uneconomical routes are operated to maintain connectivity 
to remote and rural regions. 
• As a result, Indian Railways bears a social service obligation exceeding ₹ 
40,000 crore annually. 
• The expenditure is increasing year on year on account of: 
o Periodic increases in pay and allowances 
o Fresh recruitments 
o Higher maintenance costs due to addition of new assets 
o Repayment of the COVID -related loan from the Ministry of Finance 
(MoF) 
• Despite substantial fixed and rising obligations, Indian Railways 
consistently generates operational surplus through: 
o Strong freight performance 
o Improved asset utilization 
o Cost rationalization 
• Since 2022 –23, Railways has undertaken record levels of capital 
expenditure (capex) focused on: 
o New lines 
o Track doubling 

13 
 
o Electrification 
o Rolling stock expansion 
o Modern signaling systems 
These investments are long-term growth enablers, not merely expenditures. 
• Over time, enhanced capacity and efficiency from this capex are expected 
to result in: 
o Higher freight and passenger revenues 
o Improved logistics competitiveness 
o Reduced logistics costs 
o Stronger export competitiveness 
o Greater support to the national economy 
Measures to improve Internal Resources: 
   In RE 2024 -25, Railways targeted to achieve internal resource of Rs. 
2,141 cr. and against this Railway achieved Rs. 3,460 cr. internal resources. To 
increase internal resources, IR have to increase Railways’ earnings and control 
expenditure. Therefore, to increase revenue, several measures have been taken by 
Indian Railways. These include the following: 
• To increase the network capacity, rail network expansion has been taken up in 
a big way by construction of new lines, multi tracking of existing lines and 
gauge conversion of existing lines.  
▪ Removing bottlenecks in operations by yard remodeling, construction of 
bypass/chord lines, rail flyovers etc. 
▪ The construction of Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) from Ludhiana 
to Sonnagar (1,337 Km) and Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) 
from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Terminal (JNPT) to Dadri (1,506 Km) has 
completed apporx. 96% as out of total 2,843 kms, 2,741 route kms (96.4%)

“Completion & commissioning of ROB/RUB works depends on various factors 
like cooperation of State Governments in giving consent for closure of LC, 
fixing of approach alignment, approval of General Arrangement Drawing 
(GAD), land acquisition, removal of encroachment, shifting of infringing 
utilities, statutory clearances from various authorities, law and order situation 
in the area of project/work sites, duration of working season in a year for the

the completion time of the projects / works. Therefore, it is not feasible to fix 
definite timelines for completion of ROB/RUB works.  
Difficulties faced in construction of ROBs/ RUBS: LCs are safety hazard for 
both road user as well as train operations. Elimination of LC in densely 
populated urban areas is desirable to avoid inconvenience to road user. 
Generally, construction of approaches of ROB is used to be difficult due to 
various reasons enumerated as under (which were used to be generally 
responsibility of State Govt/Road owning agencies): 
• Coordination issues with the state government  
• Land acquisition requirements & Rehabilitation & resettlement 
• Forest clearance  
• Law and order situation in the area of project site, court case and public 
protest  
• Allocation of requisite funds by State Government as required. 
• Old Sanctioned cost sharing works, but stalled, due to no response 
regarding cost sharing from State Govt. 
Initiatives taken by Railways to address the problems faced during 
construction:  
• Land acquisition requirements & Rehabilitation & resettlement : New 
policy letters dated 2.3.23 & 19.08.2024 facilitate the charging cost land 
acquisition involving private land, R&R and utility shifting required for 
construction of ROB/RUB to estimate of ROB/RUBs works sanctioned 
on 100% cost of Railway.  

35 
 
• Instructions have been issued to all zonal railways for entering into 
running contracts for timely identification of utilities and fixed 
structures coming in the alignment of ROB/RUB and their early shifting 
to fast track the construction of ROB/RUB Works 
• Now Land acquisition for ROB/RUB works can be done as special 
railway project. 
• Coordination issues: As part of latest policy all ROBs/RUBs works are 
to be undertaken by single entity to the extent possible, to reduce 
coordination issues. 
• To expedite the ROB works, Joint survey with all Stakeholders 
including State Government to finalise the tentative General 
Arrangement Drawing (GAD). 
• Periodic meeting of Railway & State Government officials to resolve 
various issues related to ROB/RUB works. 
• Allocation of requisite funds by State Government :New policy letters 
dated 2.3.23 & 19.08.2024 facilitate the sanction of work for all LCs at 
the cost of Railways except on National Highway and where state 
Govt/road owning agency/Local authority wants to take up the works at 
its cost. 
• Specific Guidelines regarding for geometry for RUBs and ROBs Based 
on MoRTH/IRC guidelines situated in congested areas are being 
developed by RDSO.

Modernization and Improvement/up -gradation of Rolling Stock to enhance 
safety, convenience and comfort of passengers is a continuous and ongoing 
process on Indian Railways. 
The following new technologies have been adopted in locomotives in recent 
years:  
i) Head on Generation Technology: In HOG system electrical power is 
fed to the coaches directly from the Overhead Equipment (OHE) through 
the Locomotive. It eliminates the need for separate diesel fuelled power 
cars in trains and thus reduces the need for pulling extra coaches and also 
increases efficiency further resulting in reduction in carbon footprint.  
Indian Railways have a total of 2342 HOG compliant locomotives as in 
January 2026. 
ii) Provision of RMS on electric locos: Remote Monitoring System helps in 
remote diagnostic of the failures in the locomotives bringing down the 
failure investigation time. As in January 2026, it has been commissioned 
on about 2233 electric locomotives and 2910 diesel locomotives. 
iii) Kavach (loco equipment): Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic 
Train Protection (ATP) system. Kavach aids the loco pilot in train running 
within specified speed limits by automatic application of brakes in case it is 
exceeded to ensure safely. 
iv)  High Reach Pantographs: High Reach Pantographs are being provided to 
for seamless working in high -rise OHE territory. Till date, 5655 
locomotives have been provided with High Reach Pantographs 
pantographs. 
v) Waterless urinals: Waterless Urinals are being provided in locomotives as 
an amenity to the loco crew.  These are robust in design considering riding 
shocks and vibrations and can be retrofitted without many alterations to 
layout and without interference with working of other equipment of 
locomotive.  Till date more than 2000 locomotives have been provided 
with Urinals as in January 2026. 

44 
 
vi) LED headlight:   LED Headlights are being provided in locomotives to 
improve visibility to Loco Pilots during train operations.  7362 locomotives 
have been provided with LED Headlights. All new locomotives are being 
manufactured with LED Headlights.  Total 8718 locomotives are provided 
with LED Headlights as in January 2026.   
vii) Energy saving mode in electric locomotives:   To save Electrical Energy in 
3-phase freight locomotives (WAG9/WAG9H/WAG9HC) modification is 
being carried out in existing scheme of load distribution and ‘Energy 
Saving Mode’ has been included in software of Auxiliary converter to put 
off the auxiliary blowers of locomotives, when cooling is not required 
during the idling of locomotives.  3028 locomotives have been modified 
with this feature as in January 2026. 
Technological improvement is a continuous process. As a step towards the 
modernization of Indian Railways (IR), many technology driven projects are 
being introduced to improve upon the Safety & Productivity and to enhance 
availability, reliability, operability, maintainability of the Rolling Assets like 
Wheel Impact Load Detector (WILD) and Hot Axlebox Hot Wheel (HAHW) 
Detector/Hot Box Detector (HBD). WILD is a way -side inspection system that 
measures the impact of wheel on tracks to automatically identify the defective 
wheels in Rolling Stock and HAHW/HBD are automatic systems consisting of 
infrared sensors installed on wayside to measure the temperature of axle 
bearing box/wheel of rolling stock while in motion. 
Further, as a step towards inducting latest technology on IR, the pilot projects 
viz. Machine Vision based Inspection Systems (MVIS) and Automatic Wheel 
Profile Measurement System (AWPMS) have been taken up. The MVIS will 
generate alerts on detecting any hanging, loose or missing components of 
moving trains and AWPMS allows automatic non-contact measurement of train 
wheel profile ensuring measurement of wheel geometry and wear. 
In addition, installation of CCTV cameras in coaches and locomotives has been 
taken up to strengthen passenger security. 

45 
 
Innovation is a continuous process to Rolling Stock Manufacturing to enhance 
safety, convenience and passenger comfort. All the Production units of Indian 
Railways are International Railway Industry Standard  (IRIS) certified units 
adopting International Standards and practices in Rolling Stock manufacture. 
RDSO, the research, design and standardization organization regularly 
communicates with PUs on different modifications, alterations etc. for 
standardization across different PUs.

14.1 Strengthening, upgradation, modernisation  and improvement of track 
infrastructure is a continuous and ongoing process over Indian Railways. The 
following measures as detailed by the Ministry are being taken by Indian Railways to 
upgrade railway tracks:  
i. Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) 
rails, Wider and heavier Pre -stressed Concrete Sleepers (PSC) with elastic 
fastening, fan -shaped layout turnout on PSC sleepers and H -beam Sleepers on 
girder bridges are being used while carrying out primary track renewals.  
ii. The Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossings are being used in 
turnout renewal works.  
iii. Supply of 260m long rail panels have been increased to avoid welding of joints, 
thereby improving safety and riding quality  
iv. Thick Web Switch Expansion Joints are being used in place of earlier 
Conventional/Improved SEJs. 
v. Adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e. Flash Butt Welding.  
vi. Adoption of mechanized system for track maintenance using high output plain 
tampers and points & crossing tampers for improved maintainability & 
reliability of track.   
vii. Deployment of state -of-the-art modern machines including Rail Grinding 
Machines to further improve asset reliability. 
viii. Mechanisation of track laying activities through use of track machines like 
PQRS, TRT, T-28 etc. 
ix. Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates for enhancing safety at LC gates. 
x. Use of advanced Phased Array technology of testing of rail and welds. 
xi. Deployment of Integrated Track Monitoring Systems (ITMS) and Oscillation 
Monitoring System (OMS) for comprehensive health assessment to ascertain 
optimal maintenance requirements. 

71 
 
xii. Adoption of portable Track Measuring Trolley for continuous recording of track 
parameters in yards. 
xiii. Using web enabled Track Management System (TMS) for integration and data 
analytics of the track inspection records received through various sources to 
enable precise maintenance inputs.

78 
 
Committee decided to construct entirely on viaduct in 2016 because

16.2 The Ministry have provided the following details of research and development 
initiatives undertaken by Indian Railways/RDSO and tangible outcomes achieved in 
terms of safety, efficiency and cost reduction: 
1. Development of Kavach System for Automatic Train Protection in Indian 
Railways which is comparable to World Standards and is cost effective.  
2. New Modern Rolling Stock like Vande Bharat, Trains, VB Sleeper trains, 
Amrit Bharat Trains, and Vande Metro Trains have been developed.  
3. Other New Rolling Socks have been Developed  like Double Decker Cargo 
Liner, Treasury Vans, Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) Parcel Van with rear 
opening, Automobile Carriers Vistadome Coaches and Dining Cars. 
4. Development of 2.4 MW first Hydrogen Fuel Cell DEMU has been done by 
Research, Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO). The rake is ready and 
is awaiting Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization  (PESO) clearance at 
Northern Railway for the Hydrogen Fueling infrastructure. 
5. Semi Automatic Couplers with Crash Tube is being developed to provide 
slack free coupling in Amrit Bharat trains. This will reduce Jack -Knifing and 
jerks in trains. 
6. Comprehensive review/ framing of guidelines on issues related to Disaster 
Management leading to more reliable equipment, coordinated response and 
time sensitive response to unforeseen circumstances. 
7. Development of Emission kit for achieving US Environmental Protection 
Agency (EPA) Tier 0+ emission standards in HHP Diesel locomotives 
Presently High Horse Power (HHP) Diesel locos do not meet any emission 
norms. In June 2022, Railway Board entrusted RDSO to float EOI for supply of 
Emission kits to upgrade HHP diesel Locomotives to US EPA Tier 0+ emission 
standards. After floating Expression of Interest (EOI), RDSO developed the 
specification for the emission kits for achieving Tier 0+ emission standards.  
8. Diesel locomotive operation in USBRL (Udhampur - Srinagar - Baramulla 
Rail Link) Section 
Original Equipment Manufacturers  (OEMs) of Diesel locomotives viz M/s 
WABTEC and M/s Progress Rail were approached by Northern Railway to 

91 
 
provide a solution for running of Diesel Locomotives in harsh climatic 
conditions of USBRL section. Due to low volumes of the number of 
locomotives to be modified for the new section, both the OEMs didn't provide 
any solution. NR approached RDSO to provide a scheme for modification of 
HHP Diesel locomotives to enable them run in sub zero temp. & high altitudes. 
A detailed study was carried out and each and every system of the locomotive 
was analysed for suitability to the climate. A scheme for modification was 
developed and provided to NR enabling operation of HHP Diesel locomotives 
over USBRL. Trials were successfully conducted in December 2024 over 
USBRL with WDG4D loco and presently 20 Diesel locomotives are operating 
in USBRL section. 
9. Modification in Diesel locomotives to enhance safe operation of trains in 
ghat sections RDSO has issued instructions for modification in Diesel 
locomotives for provision of Audio Visual indication in Banker/Rear Diesel 
Locomotives for Brake Pipe (BP) pressure drop. This modification in the 
Diesel locomotive will provide additional alert to the loco pilot of the 
Banker/Rear locomotive when Braking is initiated by the loco pilot of the 
leading locomotive so that the loco pilot in Banker/rear loco can also initiate 
braking simultaneously. This enhances the safety of train operation in Ghat 
section of Railways. 
10. Three-phase Propulsion Technology  has been introduced in Distributed 
Power Rolling Stocks (DPRS) i.e EMUs/MEMUs/Vande Bharat Trainsets 
having potential for regeneration of energy to the extent of 30% resulting in 
saving of overall energy consumption and operating efficiency. 
11. Fire safety  has been improved in terms of use of HL2/HL3 compliant 
items/components as per EN 45545 for Rolling stock application.. 
12. Development of Reverse cycle Roof Mounted Packaged Unit (RMPU)  has 
been undertaken to improve the fire safety, reliability and energy efficiency.  
13. Improvement in specifications:  More than 60 Specifications have been taken 
up for upgradation during 2025 -26 to improve Safety, Operational reliability, 
efficiency and indigenization leading to cost control. 

92 
 
14. Securing arrangement:  To ensure proper securing of hanging parts and 
consignments, following safety improvements have been done: 
a. Provision of additional safety brackets for auxiliary air reservoir. 
b. Provision of lock bolts in place of rivets for securing of critical 
components of Centre Buffer Coupler. 
c. Guideline for lashing & securing of road vehicles over wagons has been 
issued. 
d. Guidelines for securing various types of steel products and other items 
over flat and open wagon has been issued. 
15. Speed enhancement and standardization for freight stock: Approx. 94% of all 
wagon designs have been made fit for operation at common higher speed of 100 
kmph in empty and 75 kmph in loaded condition. This will ensure efficient 
freight operation and standardization of wagon by reducing the number of 
variants. Modification of wagons to achieve speed of 100/75 kmph under way. 
16. Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT) as an advanced technology for 
Ultrasonic Flaw Detection (USFD) has been introduced for Rail & Rail weld 
for improving safety after R&D and field trial. Several Research and 
Development (R&D) initiatives aimed at enhancing track safety, reliability, 
speed potential, and lifecycle cost optimization, like upgradation of USFD, by 
routine quality audit of Flash Butt Welding (FBW) etc. accordingly tangible 
outcome reduction of fracture of rail, reliability of rail weld joints have been 
taken. 
17. Development of measurement techniques  for return current through rail and 
investigations on computation of rail potential rise, Drone Inspection of 
Overhead Equipment Parameters, etc. are under research stage at I ITs under 
CRR(Centre for Railway Research). 
18. Following Products were developed for efficiency and reliability  of OHE 
infrastructure: Power Quality restorer(PQR), Automatic fault locator (AFL), 
Copper-silver (Cu-Ag) and copper-magnesium (Cu-Mg) Conductors, Rail Earth 
Clamp(REC) and Transformers of different ratings to be used in 2x25 KV 
System.
